newsitem.title: UK: UK monetary meeting to go ahead on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: UK monetary meeting to go ahead on Wednesday.

text.p: Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown will meet Bank of England Governor Eddie George for their first monetary meeting on Wednesday, May 7 as scheduled, a Treasury official told Reuters on Sunday.
"It's going ahead on Wednesday as scheduled. We have not got a time for it yet, but we will let you know either on Monday or Tuesday," the official said.
The financial markets had been uncertain whether the meeting would go ahead so close to last Thursday's election although it has long been pencilled in for that date.

Now it has been confirmed, some economists expect Brown to sanction an interest rate rise immediately. George has been calling for an interest rate rise throughout this year but the outgoing Chancellor, Kenneth Clarke, ignored him.
Base rates were last raised, by a quarter-point to six percent, on October 30 last year.
The monthly monetary meeting could be one of the last under the present structure. Brown plans to establish a new, broader monetary policy committee to oversee interest rate policy.
